events.title: Umayyad forces fight the rebels of Medina at al-Harra
events.description: During the Second Fitna, Caliph Yazid I's Umayyad army under Muslim ibn Uqba fought the rebel defenders of Medina on the lava field of Harrat Waqim, north-east of the city. The battle lasted less than a day.
events.html: During the Second Fitna, Caliph Yazid I's Umayyad army under Muslim ibn Uqba fought the rebel defenders of Medina on the lava field of Harrat Waqim, north-east of the city. The battle lasted less than a day.

events.title: Alp Arslan defeats and captures Romanos IV at Manzikert
events.description: Near Manzikert in eastern Anatolia, the Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan defeated the Byzantine army and captured Emperor Romanos IV Diogenes. The battle opened Anatolia to Turkish settlement, and Byzantine appeals for help later led to the First Crusade.

events.title: Rudolf I and Ladislaus IV defeat Ottokar II on the Marchfeld
events.description: At Dürnkrut and Jedenspeigen, the German king Rudolf I of Habsburg, allied with King Ladislaus IV of Hungary, defeated and killed Ottokar II of Bohemia. The victory gave Austria and Styria to the Habsburgs, who ruled Austria until 1918.

events.title: Edward III's longbowmen defeat the French at Crécy
events.description: English archers and dismounted men-at-arms cut down repeated French cavalry charges at Crécy. The victory, with heavy losses among the French nobility, opened the way to the siege of Calais.
events.html: English archers and dismounted men-at-arms cut down repeated French cavalry charges at Crécy. The victory, with heavy losses among the French nobility, opened the way to the siege of Calais.

events.title: The Dauphin's Armagnacs destroy a Swiss force outside Basel
events.description: Outside Basel, about 1,500 Swiss Confederates attacked a far larger French army of Armagnac mercenaries under the Dauphin Louis, the future Louis XI, and were almost entirely destroyed. Their resistance impressed the Dauphin, who withdrew and made peace.

events.title: France adopts the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
events.description: The National Assembly proclaimed that men are born free and equal in rights, and that sovereignty rests with the nation. The declaration became a founding text of modern human rights.
events.html: The National Assembly proclaimed that men are born free and equal in rights, and that sovereignty rests with the nation. The declaration became a founding text of modern human rights.

events.title: Krakatoa begins its cataclysmic eruption
events.description: The volcano of Krakatoa in the Sunda Strait began its climactic eruption, culminating in explosions the next day heard thousands of kilometres away. Tsunamis killed more than 36,000 people.
events.html: The volcano of Krakatoa in the Sunda Strait began its climactic eruption, culminating in explosions the next day heard thousands of kilometres away. Tsunamis killed more than 36,000 people.

events.title: The 19th Amendment is certified, giving US women the vote
events.description: Secretary of State Bainbridge Colby certified the 19th Amendment, barring denial of the vote on account of sex. It crowned a campaign launched at Seneca Falls in 1848.

events.title: Albino Luciani is elected Pope John Paul I
events.description: The Patriarch of Venice became the first pope to take a double name, honouring his two predecessors. Known as the 'smiling pope', he died after just 33 days.
